name: GA-09
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with a -17 point partisan lean
Incumbent Andrew Clyde running for re-election
Challenger Caitlyn Gegen has raised only about $43,000 with minimal cash on hand
Prediction markets price Democratic chances at roughly 4%
model.rationale: The district's -17 point partisan lean, Clyde's incumbency, and his large fundraising advantage over Gegen all point to a comfortable Republican hold, and prediction markets agree at about a 4% Democratic chance. With no polls or expert ratings available, the forecast rests on these fundamentals, which align closely with the baseline.
model.watch: A major outside-spending surge for Gegen or an unexpected scandal involving Clyde could narrow the margin, though a Democratic win remains a long shot.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Andrew Clyde seeks re-election in a northeastern Georgia district that leans Republican by about 17 points. He holds a large financial edge, having raised roughly $671,000 to Caitlyn Gegen's $43,000, and enters the race with the advantages of incumbency in a favorable environment for his party. Outside spending has been modest and roughly balanced on his side of the race.

Gegen faces steep structural headwinds with little money and no polling or expert attention to suggest the race is competitive. Prediction markets give her only about a 4% chance of winning. The seat is expected to remain safely in Republican hands, though the absence of polling leaves some room for uncertainty about the exact margin.
